db-relational-sql.title: Relational Model & Advanced SQL
db-relational-sql.intro: Normalization judgment, join algebra, window functions, constraints as design tools — SQL fluency beyond CRUD.
groups: Normalization & When to Break It

• 1NF atomic values → 2NF no partial dependency on composite keys → 3NF no transitive dependencies → BCNF every determinant a candidate key.
• Denormalize deliberately: read-optimized summaries (materialized counters), embedded JSON for schema-flex blobs queried whole, star schemas for analytics — each with a sync strategy stated.
• Anomaly vocabulary: update/insert/delete anomalies justify decomposition in interviews.
• Practical middle ground: normalize OLTP core, denormalize at edges (caches, read models); document sync paths (triggers, CDC, app-level dual-write w/ outbox).
• Trick question prep: 'is 3NF always right?' — No: report-heavy workloads trade write cost for read joins consciously.
Join Algebra & Semantics

• Inner/left/right/full/cross + self joins; semi-join (EXISTS) vs anti-join (NOT EXISTS) semantics — anti-join NULL trap with NOT IN vs NOT EXISTS classic.
• Join algorithms under the hood: nested loop (small outer × indexed inner), hash join (build+probe, memory-bound spills), merge join (pre-sorted inputs) — planner picks by size/stats; knowing this explains 'why is my join slow'.
• LATERAL joins: correlated per-row subqueries with set returns (top-N-per-group elegantly).
• Multi-way join ordering matters exponentially naive — planner prunes via stats; stale stats = catastrophic orders.
• Join filter placement: WHERE vs ON differs ONLY for outer joins (WHERE on right of LEFT JOIN silently converts to inner!) — favorite gotcha probe.
Window Functions Mastery

• OVER(PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ...): aggregates WITHOUT collapsing rows; running totals (ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), moving averages.
• Ranking trio: ROW_NUMBER (unique), RANK (ties share, gaps), DENSE_RANK (ties share, no gaps) — dedupe-latest pattern: qualify row_number()=1 per partition.
• LAG/LEAD for deltas/sessionization: gap > X minutes starts new session (event-data staple).
• NTILE buckets, FIRST_VALUE/LAST_VALUE frame gotchas (default frame is RANGE UNBOUNDED PRECEDING..CURRENT ROW — specify ROWS explicitly!).
• CTEs: WITH for readability; RECURSIVE for org charts/graph walks; materialization behavior varies (PG12+ inlines unless MATERIALIZED).
Constraints & Data Integrity

• PK/FK/UNIQUE/CHECK/NOT NULL/DEFAULT — declarative integrity beats application hope; FK indexing reminder (unindexed FKs lock-spike parents).
• DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED constraints solve circular references and bulk-load ordering.
• Partial + expression indexes as constraint superpowers: UNIQUE(active_row_flag) WHERE active; unique(lower(email)).
• Exclusion constraints (Postgres): no-overlapping room bookings with GiST range types — constraint-as-invariant flex few candidates know.
• Triggers vs constraints vs app logic: prefer constraints (optimizer-aware, race-free), triggers for audit/CDC side-effects only.
Advanced Query Patterns

• Upserts: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE with excluded.* refs; concurrent upsert uniqueness requirements (conflict target must match a real unique index).
• Hierarchies: adjacency list + recursive CTE vs materialized path (ltree!) vs closure table — tradeoffs query-time vs write-time.
• Time-series idioms: date_trunc buckets + generate_series to fill gaps; windowed deltas; BRIN on event_time.
• Full-text: tsvector/tsquery, GIN indexes, ranking ts_rank, websearch_to_tsquery UX; pg_trgm for fuzzy/autocomplete.
• Pivot/unpivot: FILTER (COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ...)), crosstab extension; JSON aggregation jsonb_agg for API-shaped responses straight from SQL.
SQL Interview Drills

• Second-highest salary (OFFSET 1 LIMIT 1 after DISTINCT ORDER BY DESC / dense_rank variant) — warmup.
• Top-N-per-group (LATERAL or window) — mid-level staple; explain why window version scans once.
• Month-over-month growth (LAG), sessionization (gap logic), retention cohort matrix (self-join + date_trunc grid).
• Find duplicates + keep latest (row_number delete pattern) — operational realism.
• Consecutive-events detection (gaps-and-islands: row_number - row_number partition trick) — senior-tier signal when unprompted.

db-indexing-storage.title: Indexing & Storage Engines
db-indexing-storage.intro: B-trees vs LSMs, composite index rules, page layout — the #1 database interview topic done properly.
groups: B-Tree Mechanics

• Sorted keys in page-sized nodes, fanout ~100-500 → height 3-4 covers billions of rows; log_fanout(N) reads per lookup.
• Point lookup descends root→leaf; ranges follow leaf sibling chains; splits propagate top-down, lazy deletion leaves holes reclaimed later.
• Clustered vs secondary: InnoDB PK IS the table (leaf holds row); secondaries store PK pointer. Postgres heap separate; ALL indexes secondary (ctid) — updates touch every index unless HOT applies.
• Sequential keys fill pages ~100%; random UUIDs split mid-page (~50% fill) → bloat + cache misses — ordered IDs (ULID/snowflake/UUIDv7) fix it.
• Page internals flavor: slotted arrays (slot directory + growing-from-end tuples), checksums, WAL-before-page rule.
LSM-Trees & Compaction

• Path: WAL → memtable(skiplist) → flushed SSTable run; reads probe memtable then runs newest-first, bloom filters gate disk probes.
• Size-tiered compaction merges similar runs (write-friendly, space/read-unfriendly overlap) vs leveled (non-overlapping levels, ratio ~10 — bounded read amp, heavier rewrite).
• Amplification triangle: optimize write/read/space — pick two-ish; LSM wins write-heavy sequential IO, B-tree wins read-heavy + strong scan locality.
• Tombstones linger until bottommost compaction; TTL compactions expire; merge operators push RMW into storage (RocksDB style).
· Knobs interviewers probe: bloom bits/key (~10 ≈1% FP), memtable count/size (L0 stall!), block cache, compaction throughput caps, WAL placement on separate volume.
Composite Index Strategy

• Left-prefix rule; equality columns first, ONE range column last (range kills subsequent seeks).
• ORDER BY satisfaction: matching sequence/direction after fixed-equality prefix avoids sort nodes; mixed ASC/DESC needs explicit column directions.
• Covering: INCLUDE padding columns → index-only scans skip heap (PG visibility-map permitting; vacuum freshness matters!).
• Uniqueness granularity: unique(a,b) constrains pairs; partial UNIQUE ... WHERE active encodes 'one active X per Y' business rules at engine level.
• Expression/GIN/trgm toolbox: lower(email), jsonb paths, full-text vectors, similarity search — pick narrowest correct type.
Storage Pages, Buffers & IO

• Fixed pages (8KB PG/16KB InnoDB) unit of cache+IO; buffer pools evict via clock-sweep/approx-LRU; dirty pages flushed under WAL-first discipline.
• Read-ahead heuristics for scans; random access punishes spinning disks historically, NVMe softens but cache still rules.
• Checksums end-to-end (page-level corruption detection), torn-page protection via full-page images in WAL.
• Compression: page-level (TORN safety), columnar stores compress 10x+ (Parquet dictionaries/RLE) — OLAP column stores explained briefly (C-store lineage → Snowflake/Redshift/BigQuery).
• Dual write-path choice: DB-managed cache + O_DIRECT vs OS page cache trust — Postgres vs MySQL culture split, know both arguments.
Index Maintenance Reality

• Every index taxes writes; audit unused (pg_stat_user_indexes idx_scan≈0) before adding more.
• Bloat from MVCC dead tuples → REINDEX CONCURRENTLY/pg_repack online; autovacuum per-table tuning for churny tables.
• HOT updates (PG): unchanged indexed cols + page room → skip index writes entirely (fillfactor tuning enables headroom).
• Online DDL spectrum: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY (two passes, no long locks), instant/inplace algorithms (MySQL 8), logical-backfill patterns for big rewrites.
• Monitoring: index usage histograms, bloat estimates, invalid indexes post-failed-builds (drop them), duplicate index detection (same leading columns).
Worked Scenarios Bank

• Deep pagination slow → keyset seek predicate on (created_at,id); OFFSET skips count-rows expensively.
• ILIKE '%x%' seq-scans → trigram GIN or external search; typo tolerance needs ngrams/edit distance layer.
• Multi-tenant noise → lead composites with tenant_id + partition pruning by tenant.
• Dashboard GROUP BY crawl → incremental summary tables/materialized views refreshed incrementally; time-bucket + BRIN for raw scans.
• Write cliff after 'small feature' → new index on hot table + random UUID PK page splits; ordered-key migration plan narrated.

db-transactions-mvcc.title: Transactions, Isolation & MVCC
db-transactions-mvcc.intro: ACID beyond acronyms: anomaly zoo, snapshot internals, locking strategy, recovery plumbing.
groups: Isolation Anomalies Catalog

• Dirty read (uncommitted visible), non-repeatable read (re-read changed), phantom (predicate result grows).
• Lost update: read-modify-write races — counter increments without atomic UPDATE or SELECT FOR UPDATE.
• Write skew: two txns read each other's data, write disjoint rows, jointly violate invariant (on-call doctors!) — the SERIALIZABLE poster child; FKs won't catch it.
• Read skew: transfer sees debit without credit — snapshot isolation fixes within-txn consistency.
• Level mapping truth: PG READ COMMITTED (per-statement snapshots), REPEATABLE READ = snapshot isolation (blocks phantoms too), SERIALIZABLE adds SSI killing write skew; MySQL RR adds gap locks instead.
MVCC Internals (Postgres lens)

• Tuples carry xmin/xmax; snapshots = horizon + in-progress list; visibility check picks your version — writers never block readers.
• UPDATE inserts new version + marks old xmax; DELETE marks xmax only; VACUUM reclaims dead versions eventually.
• Long-running transactions pin the xmin horizon → table/index bloat explosion — production incident generator #1; monitor oldest xid age.
• Wraparound: 32-bit xids; freeze old tuples so horizon advances; ignored warnings force shutdown — cite the real outage class.
• InnoDB contrast: undo logs reconstruct old versions, purge thread cleans; RR uses read views similarly but locking differs (gap locks).
Locking Strategies

• 2PL classic: acquire as-needed, hold till commit — serializability via blocking; deadlock detection via wait-for graph kills victims.
• Row modes: FOR UPDATE / FOR SHARE / FOR KEY SHARE gradations protect FK references; NOWAIT fails fast; SKIP LOCKED powers job queues without coordination (the modern queue answer!).
• Lock queues are FIFO with fairness starvation quirks: one ALTER ACCESS EXCLUSIVE behind a long reader blocks ALL newcomers behind IT — lock_timeout + retry discipline mandatory for migrations.
• Advisory locks: app-named keys for leader election/migration guards — cheaper than fake-row tricks.
• Hot-row contention: last-insert-id sequences serialize; mitigate per-shard sequences, batched ID ranges, or queue-writes.
Recovery: WAL & ARIES Ideas

• WAL rule: log hits stable storage BEFORE data pages ever do; steal/no-force policies enable both flexibility and correctness.
• ARIES phases: Analysis (losers/dirty set) → Redo (repeat history forward from checkpoint) → Undo (compensation records, idempotent across crash-during-recovery).
• Group commit batches fsyncs across committers — throughput jump, slight p99 rise; commit_delay knobs.
• Checkpoints bound replay; fuzzy checkpoints avoid stalls; full_page_images heal torn pages.
• Replication synergy: same WAL stream feeds PITR archives, streaming replicas, logical decoding (CDC) — slot management prevents unbounded retention (disk-fill incidents!).
Distributed Transactions Preview

• 2PC prepare→commit: coordinator failure blocks in-doubt txns — availability tax; XA legacy pain stories.
• Sagas: local txn chain + compensations; choreography (events) vs orchestration (Temporal-style coordinator); compensations idempotent + retryable by contract.
• Outbox pattern: state-change + event written atomically locally, relay publishes — kills dual-write inconsistency; Debezium reads the outbox via CDC.
• Exactly-once is an illusion end-to-end: dedupe keys + idempotent consumers make it LOOK once; say this sentence verbatim in interviews.
• Consensus-backed commit (Spanner/Calvin/percolator flavors) when cross-shard invariants non-negotiable — price: latency + ops complexity.
Anomaly Hunt Drill Set

• Ticket oversell → unique(concert,user) constraint or SERIALIZABLE or advisory-lock keyed concert_id — three valid answers, rank them.
• Balance transfer skew → single txn + row locks; invariant sum constant asserted.
• Counter drift ORM RMW → atomic UPDATE n=n+1 RETURNING n.
• Multi-query report inconsistency → wrap in REPEATABLE READ explicitly.
• Migration deadlock between deploys → standardize lock order, timeouts, retries; runbook documentation closes it permanently.

db-query-optimization.title: Query Optimization
db-query-optimization.intro: Think like the planner: statistics, plan shapes, EXPLAIN reading, and rewrite playbooks for slow queries.
groups: Planner Cost Model Essentials

• Seq scan cheap/page but reads all; index scan pays random-access penalty (random_page_cost=4 default — drop to ~1.1 on SSD/NVMe!); bitmap scans bridge (index → sorted page list → heap pass).
• Join selection: nested loop (small outer, indexed inner), hash (medium unsorted, memory-bounded spills to temp), merge (pre-sorted giants).
• Statistics drive everything: n_distinct, MCV lists, histograms; ANALYZE after bulk loads; correlated-column misestimates fixed via extended statistics (CREATE STATISTICS PG10+).
• Constants matter: sargability — functions on indexed columns disable seeks (rewrite date_trunc(ts)=X as range predicates); implicit casts, leading wildcards same disease.
• Parallel plans: gather/gather-merge nodes, workers per gather capped; small tables stay serial deliberately.
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) Fluency

• Read top-down tree; compare ESTIMATED vs ACTUAL rows — divergence flags stats problems; loops multiplier on inner nodes multiplies costs.
• BUFFERS: shared hit (cache) vs read (IO!) vs written; temp blocks = spill-to-disk (work_mem too low for sort/hash).
• Node red flags: Sort (spilled), Materialize (memory copies), Nested Loop with huge inner loops, Filter removing most rows late.
• Timing skew inside nodes (actual time spans) reveals sub-node culprits; track where wall-clock concentrates.
· Tools: explain.dalibo.com visualizer, auto_explain logging slow plans with buffers, hypopg tests hypothetical indexes WITHOUT building them — killer demo answer.
Rewrite Playbook (Top Offenders)

• SELECT * → project needed cols (enables covering scans, cuts IO); ORM defaults murder performance — name the N+1 problem and eager-loading fix.
• OR-chains across columns → UNION ALL of indexed branches or bitmaps; LIKE '%x%' → trigram/search engine; DISTINCT band-aids → fix join fan-out root cause.
• Correlated scalar subqueries per row → lateral/window/join rewrite; function-on-column predicates → expression index or sargable rewrite.
• Pagination OFFSET deep → keyset; COUNT(*) for pagination UI → approximate counts or cursor existence checks.
• Big IN lists → temp-table join or = ANY(array); batch DELETEs loop bounded chunks avoiding long transactions/bloat.
Statistics & Maintenance Levers

• Autovacuum analyze cadence per churn; manual ANALYZE post-bulk-load; default target 100 samples×300 — raise for skewed distributions.
• Extended statistics objects: functional dependencies, ndistinct, MCV-lists combos — fixes 'city+street correlation' misestimates.
• Plan stability: plan_cache_mode for pathological generic-vs-custom plans (prepared statements), pg_hint_plan escape hatch when planner wrong NOW (document debt!).
• Partitioning as optimization: prune at plan/exec time; attach/detach rolls windows instantly; partition-wise joins when aligned.
• Resource guards: statement_timeout per role, work_mem per-query sizing, idle_in_transaction_session_timeout killing horizon-pinning zombies.
Schema-Level Optimizations

• Data typing: text vs varchar identical perf; numeric exactness vs float8 speed; enum vs lookup FK tradeoffs; timestamptz ALWAYS (timezone bugs are data corruption).
• JSONB: containment operators @> with GIN; expression indexes for hot paths; TOAST compression choices (lz4/zstd) for fat columns.
• Denormalized counters maintained trigger-side or async rollups — read latency vs consistency budget decided consciously.
• Archive tiers: hot NVMe recent partitions, cold object-storage exports queryable via FDW/external tables — lifecycle policy narrative.
• Connection architecture: pooler modes (session/transaction), prepared-statement caveats under transaction pooling, max_connections math vs RAM.
Case Clinic Narratives

• 'Report times out' → missing composite + spilled sorts + OFFSET; deliver keyset + covering index + pre-aggregated summary layered answer.
• 'Sudden regression after data grew' → plan flip at stats threshold; ANALYZE, verify with explain, add extended stats, consider hint bridge.
• 'ORM N+1 storm under load' → measure query counts per request, dataloader/eager patterns, cache hot entities, budget remaining queries.
• 'Vacuum can't keep up' → tune autovacuum cost limits per table, reduce index count on churny tables, consider partition-drop vs delete strategies.
• 'Replica queries slow while primary fine' → replay lag + hot-standby conflicts; hot_standby_feedback tradeoff, max_standby_streaming_delay, route heavy analytics elsewhere.

db-replication-sharding.title: Replication & Sharding
db-replication-sharding.intro: Scale-out fundamentals: replication modes, shard key strategy, rebalancing choreography, ID generation.
groups: Replication Modes Tradeoffs

• Sync waits replica ack: zero-loss, latency floor = slowest ack, availability coupled. Async: fast, failover loses tail (RPO>0).
• Semi-sync middle ground; PG synchronous_commit ladder off→on→remote_write→remote_flush→remote_apply (apply = causality visible on replica!).
• Failover machinery: promotion timelines/history divergence (PG), quorum/fencing against split-brain, client rerouting layers (pooler/DNS/driver discovery).
• Lag monitoring: byte LSN delta + seconds-behind; hot_standby_feedback tradeoff (bloat primary vs canceled replica queries).
• Read-your-writes routing: store LSN/token after write, pin reads until replica catches up — the standard fix interviewers want named.
Shard Key Doctrine

• Range shards: ordered scans natural, monotonic-key hotspot risk (time-series hammers last shard).
• Hash shards: uniform spread, lose range locality; consistent hashing minimizes movement on resize; compound hash(tenant)+range(time) hybrid best-of-both.
• Lookup-directory: flexible placement, extra hop + HA story for the map itself.
• Instagram doctrine (cite!): thousands of LOGICAL shards mapped onto few physical servers upfront — resharding becomes moving logical units; shard-id embedded in IDs day-one.
• Cross-shard reality: scatter-gather latency = slowest shard; per-shard secondary indexes only; global indexes/denormalized read models for non-key lookups.
Rebalancing & Migration Choreography

• Dual-write during transition, backfill historical data, verify with checksum comparisons, shadow-read diffing, THEN shift traffic gradually per shard-unit.
• Cutover mechanics: config-driven routing flips, rollback plans rehearsed, error budgets defined before starting.
• Reshard storms: throttled movers respect production IO budgets; rate-limit backfills like backups.
• Schema evolution during sharding: additive-only changes, versioned readers/writers, contract tests across versions.
• War-story framing: 'we moved 40% of data with zero customer-visible errors because verification gates preceded traffic shifts' — process maturity signal.
ID Generation Under Shards

• Auto-increment breaks → snowflake 64-bit: timestamp|machine|sequence — sortable, unique, embeds origin; clock-skew handling (wait/rotate machine bits).
• Instagram variant: shard-id in high bits via PG sequence trick — bigint compatible, routes directly (one-hop lookups).
• UUIDv4 random: B-tree-hostile page splits everywhere; UUIDv7 time-ordered prefix fixes locality (2024+ standardization momentum); ULID/CUID cousins.
• Flickr ticket servers: central counter simplicity vs SPOF-ish scaling ceiling — fine at moderate scale, honest tradeoff framing.
• Selection rubric: sortability aids pagination/cache; embedded shard-id aids routing; randomness aids security tokens (never snowflakes for secrets!).
Consistency Models Applied

• Linearizability strongest (consensus-priced); sequential/causal cheaper; eventual + session guarantees (read-your-writes, monotonic reads) what most systems actually offer.
• PACELC reframing: partition forces AP/CP; else latency-vs-consistency persists forever — use the acronym correctly.
• CRDT convergence without coordination for counters/sets/registers — collaborative editing, offline carts; Riak/Redis-Enterprise heritage.
• Feature-to-consistency mapping: inventory checkout strong; feed/timeline eventual; profile display name causal-ish — articulate per-feature budgets.
• Jepsen literacy: name a famous finding (Mongo lost-writes era, ES pause-resume divergence) to show you follow the anomaly literature.
Capacity Math Drills

• Nodes ≈ QPS × row_bytes × RF ÷ node_capacity × 1.4 headroom; rebuild capacity = survive N-1 loss.
• Celebrity fan-out: write-time (precompute timelines) vs read-time (merge on open) — Twitter's published hybrid threshold by follower count; quote it.
• Retention tiering: hot SSD 7d → warm 90d → object cold → archive; purge jobs vs partition drops.
• Pooling math: pods × conns vs max_connections → pgbouncer transaction mode; prepared statements caveats.
• Cost lens: egress shaping multi-region choices, NVMe replicas pricing, managed-vs-self break-evens — $ fluency lands well.

db-nosql-newsql.title: NoSQL & NewSQL Landscape
db-nosql-newsql.intro: Document, KV, wide-column, graph, search, vector + consensus-native NewSQL — picking engines by workload, not hype.
groups: Document Stores (MongoDB focus)

• Model: BSON docs, embedded-vs-reference decision = aggregate boundary question (accessed together → embed; unbounded growth → reference+bucket).
• Indexes similar theory (B-tree); covered queries, multikey array indexes; aggregation pipeline vs SQL mental remap.
• Transactions: single-doc atomic historically; multi-doc ACID since 4.0 (replica sets)/4.2 (sharded) — cite versions to show currency.
• Sharding: hashed vs ranged keys, zone sharding for geo; mongos routing layer; chunk balancing history → rebalance v2 improvements.
• Honest weaknesses to volunteer: join-light modeling pushes app-side assembly; Jepsen history (lost writes pre-majority-era) fixed but reputation lingers — balanced takes impress.
KV & Wide-Column (Redis/Dynamo/Cassandra)

• Redis: in-mem data structures (lists/sets/zsets/streams/HLL/bitmaps!) — zset leaderboard idiom; persistence RDB snapshots + AOF logs; cluster slots hashing; pub/sub vs streams durability distinction.
• DynamoDB: partition-key (+sort key) design IS everything; hot-partition avoidance, adaptive capacity; on-demand vs provisioned economics; global tables eventual multi-region.
• Cassandra/Dynamo lineage: consistent hashing ring, tunable consistency (QUORUM math), LSM storage, tombstone/compaction care; partition design avoiding wide partitions (10s of MB limit guidance).
• ScyllaDB: C++ rewrite, thread-per-core sharding — Discord migration story (trillions of messages, p99 gains) as case study.
• Anti-pattern callouts: unbounded partitions, read-before-write RMW under contention, secondary-index abuse (local indexes = scatter).
Graph & Search Engines

• Graph (Neo4j/property-graph, Cypher; JanusGraph/TinkerPop): relationship-heavy domains (fraud rings, social graphs, recommendations) — index-free adjacency means O(degree) hops vs recursive SQL joins.
• When NOT graph: mostly-aggregate workloads — relational wins; honest scoping scores points.
• Elasticsearch/OpenSearch: inverted index, analyzers, scoring BM25, aggregations; near-realtime refresh interval; shard sizing ~10-50GB guidance.
• Ops realities: deep pagination (scroll/search_after), rebalance pains, mapping explosions, JVM heaps ≤31GB compressed-oops lore.
• Hybrid stack pattern: system-of-record in Postgres → CDC → search index projection — reconciliation + rebuild tooling part of the pitch.
Vector Stores & Embedding Era

• Embeddings: high-dim vectors; similarity via cosine/dot; ANN indexes HNSW (graph-based, great recall/speed, memory-hungry) vs IVFFlat (cluster-pruned, train step).
• pgvector inside Postgres: HNSW support, hybrid keyword+semantic rerank pipelines — 'start in your existing DB' pragmatic answer.
• Dedicated engines (Pinecone/Qdrant/Milvus/weaviate): sharding, replication, metadata filtering maturity; payload filters interplay with ANN traversal.
• Recall@k vs QPS vs RAM triangle; quantization (product/PQ, scalar) trades accuracy for footprint.
• RAG architecture sound-bite: ingestion → chunking → embedding → index; query → retrieve → rerank → generate; freshness via CDC re-embedding jobs.
NewSQL & Consensus-Native

• Spanner: globally distributed, TrueTime GPS/atomic clocks → external consistency via commit-wait; Paxos groups per shard; quote the exotic hardware honestly.
• CockroachDB: Raft ranges, SQL on top, serializable default; hotspot handling via split ranges; multi-region table-locality controls.
• TiDB/Vitess contrast: MySQL-compatible scaling layers (proxy/shard orchestration) vs monolithic NewSQL — migration-path considerations dominate real decisions.
• FoundationDB: deterministic simulation testing legend — testing-culture talking point transcending products.
• Adoption calculus: operational simplicity of one system vs proven-tool composition; migrations priced honestly.
Selection Framework (The Answer Template)

• Interrogate workload: shape (relational/doc/KV/graph/vectors), scale (rows/QPS), consistency needs (money vs feed), latency targets, team familiarity, ops appetite.
• Default posture: Postgres until evidence says otherwise — boring-tech-wins narrative with concrete thresholds (when shards/replcas actually needed).
• Polyglot persistence reality: core relational + Redis cache + search projection + queue — integration costs counted honestly.
• Escape hatches: read replicas, caching, archiving, partitioning often defer 'need NoSQL' conclusions years.
• Close with migration reversibility: avoid data-model lock-ins hard to leave; export paths tested — senior judgment signature.

db-distributed-db.title: Distributed Databases
db-distributed-db.intro: Consensus storage, quorum math, geo-topologies, and the anomaly literature — depth tier for infra-flavored rounds.
groups: Quorum Systems Math

• R/W/N: reads need R replicas, writes W; consistency requires R+W>N (intersection); typical N=3,R=2,W=2.
• Sloppy quorums + hinted handoff (Dynamo) prioritize availability during node loss — divergence possible, reconciliation later.
• Leaderless read repair/anti-entropy (Merkle trees) converge state eventually; last-write-wins timestamps = clock-trust gamble (vector clocks alternative complexity).
• Latency tail: quorum RTT = slowest-of-R sampling — p99 dominated by straggler probability; tail-tolerant reads (read one + repair async) trade freshness.
• Contrast with consensus: quorums alone give eventual-ish guarantees; linearizability needs leader sequencing + lease/fencing discipline.
Raft-Powered Storage Internals

• Per-range/per-shard Raft groups (Cockroach ranges ~512MB, TiKV regions): log replication → FSM apply → snapshot catch-up for lagging followers.
• Lease-based reads: leader leases avoid quorum round per read; clock-skew bounds assumed — fencing tokens guard split-brain windows.
• Split/merge mechanics: range splits at size/threshold, raft groups fork; merges rarer (complexity) — rebalancing moves replicas respecting locality constraints.
• Recovery narratives: follower crash → log replay; majority loss → unavailable not corrupt (CP posture); restore-from-backup drills as first-class features.
• Compare ETCD (consensus meta-store) vs storage engines using consensus internally — layered architecture clarity.
Geo-Distribution Patterns

• Regional replicas async: reads local-fresh-enough, single write region — simplest global posture; DR story solid.
• Quorum-across-regions (CRDB/Spanner): write latency includes cross-region consensus RTTs (100ms+ transcontinental) — product tolerance required.
• Follow-the-sun: leaseholder migration by daylight; home-region pinning for user-owned entities balances latency/legal.
• Conflict policy menu: LWW clocks (danger), region-authoritative entities, CRDT merge, app-level merge UIs — choose per entity class.
• Compliance partitioning: EU-data-stays-EU via regional table locality — legal constraints shape topology before performance does.
Anomaly Literature (Jepsen Literacy)

• Stale reads classes: monotonic-atomic-view violations, bounded staleness breaches under load-shedding.
• Lost-update families: read-modify-write races surviving claimed isolation levels; CAS loops without fencing still race post-pause.
• Pause/resume + clocks: VM freezes past lease expiry — Fencing tokens (monotonic storage-issued) invalidate zombie writers; Kleppmann's 'leading the ticks' essay reference.
• Famous findings to cite loosely: Mongo majority-commit-default evolution, Elasticsearch pause-resume divergence, ZooKeeper client-cache staleness nuance.
• Takeaway stance: 'trust measured behavior + formal-ish specs (TLA+) over marketing isolation claims' — maturity marker.
Backups, PITR & DR Realism

• 3-2-1 updated for DB world: continuous WAL shipping (PITR to any second), cross-region encrypted copies, quarterly RESTORE rehearsals (untested backup = no backup).
• RPO/RTO arithmetic drives spend: async replication seconds-RPO vs sync zero-RPO premium.
• Logical vs physical restores: point-in-time container spin-up for forensic queries; schema/version compatibility matrices during upgrades.
• Corruption scenarios: logical bug replicates faithfully — need pre-corruption recovery windows; delayed replicas as time-machine insurance.
• Game-day script sample: kill region → promote → verify app SLOs → failback choreography — narrate having RUN one.
Emerging Topics Worth Name-Dropping

• Deterministic databases (Calvin): pre-ordered transactions eliminate 2PC/locks — throughput marvels, interactive-latency tradeoffs.
• Serverless databases (Neon/Aurora-style separation): compute/storage split, scale-to-zero, branchable copy-on-write DBs for dev/CI — changing test-data workflows.
• HTAP architectures: row OLTP + columnar replica analytic mirrors (TiFlash-style) — one-system analytics dreams vs mature ELT stacks.
• Confidential computing DBs: enclave-encrypted processing (always-encrypted evolution) — regulated-industry angle.
• Formal methods mainstreaming: TLA+ specs for replication protocols cited in eng blogs — hiring-bar signal at top shops.
resources: Kleppmann — How to do distributed locking

db-caching-redis.title: Caching & Redis Internals
db-caching-redis.intro: Cache strategies that survive production plus Redis internals: structures, persistence, clustering, pitfalls.
groups: Cache Pattern Playbook

• Cache-aside default: read miss → load → SET with TTL; write path updates DB then invalidates (not updates!) — invalidation avoids races writing stale values concurrently.
• Read-through/write-through/write-behind distinctions; write-behind loses-tail risk accepted for write-heavy counters sometimes.
• TTL doctrine: staleness budget per feature; jitter TTLs ±20% preventing synchronized expiry herds.
• Stampede defenses: request coalescing/singleflight (one loader, waiters share), probabilistic early expiration (XFetch formula), locks with timeout fallback-to-origin.
• Negative caching: cache misses/not-founds briefly (auth lookups hammered with garbage) — often-missed trick worth naming.
Eviction & Memory Policy

• Policies: allkeys-lru default-ish; volatile-* only-expiring-keys; LFU (redis 4+) better fits skewed popularity; noeviction for pure durable usage.
• Maxmemory accounting excludes fragmentation/replication buffers — OOM surprises despite policy; monitor used_memory vs RSS gap.
• Key hygiene: no KEYS * (O(N) freeze!) — SCAN cursors; hash-slot friendly multi-op via pipelines/MSET; expiration is lazy+active mix.
• Big-key surgery: --bigkeys scan, DEL of millions-of-members blocks — UNLINK async reclaim; HSCAN-trim patterns.
• Memory math example: 1M string keys ~90B overhead each baseline — estimate before capacity planning; ziplist/listpack thresholds compact small collections.
Redis Internals Worth Knowing

• Single-threaded command execution (IO threads for parsing since 6) — atomicity free, beware O(N) commands; why Lua scripts give multi-key atomicity.
• Event loop epoll; pipelining amortizes RTTs massively (10x+ throughput); RESP protocol simplicity.
• Persistence duo: RDB fork+COW snapshots (fast restarts, gap risk) + AOF append (everysec fsync default, rewrite compaction); hybrid 4.0+.
• Replication async → failover loses tail; sentinel vs cluster: managed failover vs sharded P2P gossip (16384 slots).
• Cluster routing: MOVED/ASK redirects, hash-tags {user123} forcing co-location for multi-key ops; resharding online slot migration.
Data Structure Idioms

• Leaderboards: ZADD/ZREVRANGE with scores; rate windows: INCR + EXPIRE vs sorted-set timestamp trimming (sliding precision).
• Sessions: hash per session + TTL refresh touch; distributed locks SET NX PX + token-value release-script (Redlock controversy awareness: Kleppmann critique, Martin–Salvatore debate).
• Streams: consumer groups, acks, pending-entry claims — Kafka-lite semantics in-process; XADD maxlen trimming.
• HyperLogLog cardinality (0.81% err @12KB), bitmap signins (SETBIT day offsets), geospatial GEO commands (geohash-backed).
• Pub/sub fire-and-forget vs streams/lists durability choice — articulate per use-case.
Caching Architecture Tiers

• Layer cake: browser/service-worker → CDN edge → app-local LRU (microseconds, tiny) → shared Redis (sub-ms) → DB. Local caches need bus invalidation or short TTLs (multi-pod coherence!).
• Consistency spectrum: strict (transactional outbox + invalidation stream) vs eventual (pub/sub notifications, best-effort) — pick per entity.
• Hot-key mitigation: replica reads, local mirror of ultra-hot keys, splitting composite keys; celebrity-event runbooks.
• Cold-start warming: preload critical keys on deploy/scale-up; synthetic traffic reheats caches pre-marketing-events.
• Failure postures: cache-down = origin flood risk → shed/degrade endpoints, static fallback payloads, autoscale triggers keyed on hit-ratio collapse.
Interview Scenario Bank

• 'Design trending topics' → sliding-window counts (streams/zsets), periodic snapshot to DB, edge-cache top-K list 5s TTL.
• 'Rate limiter' → fixed-window INCR/EXPIRE simple; token bucket via Lua for burst fidelity; sharded counters for throughput; mention Redis-cell GCRA module.
• 'Session store sizing' → active users × session bytes × replication factor + headroom; eviction policy volatile-ttl; benchmark before promising SLAs.
• 'Cache coherence after DB failover' → flush-by-prefix versioned namespaces, short-TTL guard rails during incidents, reconcile jobs.
• 'Why not just cache everything?' → invalidation surface, staleness bugs, cost curves, observability burden — judgment answer over maximalism.

db-case-studies.title: Database Case Studies
db-case-studies.intro: Real production architectures retold precisely: Instagram sharding, Discord messaging, Twitter fan-out, Stripe ledgers.
groups: Instagram: Sharding at Scale

• Problem: 90+ TB photos metadata, Postgres everywhere; solution: THOUSANDS of logical shards mapped onto fewer physical EC2+PG instances upfront.
• IDs: 41-bit timestamp | 13-bit logical shard | 10-bit autoinc — bigint-compatible, routes directly to owning shard, sortable chronologically.
• Application-layer routing: code maps logical shard → physical host via config; resharding = move logical units, transparent to schema.
• Postgres-specific wins: pgbouncer pooling fleet-wide, logical backups per shard, vacuum tuned per workload; Redis zipmap memory trick for 300-byte hashes (famous blog detail).
• Transferable lesson: plan logical→physical decoupling BEFORE scale forces it; embed routing hints in identifiers.
Discord: Trillions of Messages

• Journey: MongoDB (doc-per-message) hit 500M+ msgs/day pain → Cassandra (single partition per channel, bucketed by time) → ScyllaDB (C++ thread-per-core, p99 wins, same model).
• Partition strategy: channel_id partition key + time buckets limiting partition sizes; TWCS compaction for time-series write pattern.
• Trillion-message milestone details: GC pressure management, repair scheduling around traffic, hot-channel mitigation via caching recent messages.
• Adjacent Discord posts: Elixir fan-in/out architecture, NATS/jetstream experiments, Rust read-state service — ecosystem breadth signals.
• Lesson: storage-engine fit evolves WITH workload; migration tooling (dual-reads, backfillers, cutover dashboards) is the real engineering.
Twitter: Fan-Out Economics

• Timeline generation dichotomy: write-time fan-out (push tweets into follower timelines in Redis) fast-read/expensive-celebrity vs read-time merge cheap-write/expensive-read.
• Published approach: hybrid threshold (~thousands of followers switch to read-time merge for celeb accounts); users-following-many-but-few-followers asymmetry handled.
• Early scaling war stories: Ruby GC, denormalized timelines, Memcached fleet sizing — folklore worth citing lightly.
• Modern parallels: TikTok-style algorithmic feeds abandon chronological precompute entirely → recommendation retrieval+ranking pipelines (feature stores, candidate generators) — evolution narrative impresses.
• Numbers game: 100M-follower tweet — write-time would be 100M writes; merge-on-read = per-open union over sources — quantify why threshold exists.
Stripe: Money Movement Correctness

• Ledger design: append-only double-entry journal (every transfer = debit+credit rows), immutable events, balances DERIVED via rollups not mutated.
• Idempotency everywhere: API keys stored against responses, replays return originals — network-retry-safe payments (their famous idempotency blog).
• Distributed coordination: sagas for multi-service money movement, exactly-once illusions via dedupe + transactional outboxes; reconciliation jobs comparing ledger vs bank feeds nightly.
• Data platform: snapshot + change-capture into warehouse; fraud pipelines consuming same event spine.
• Interview transfer: any money-touching design should echo these primitives unprompted — instant credibility.
Netflix/Uber/WhatsApp Quick Hits

• Netflix: microservices + chaos engineering origin; EV cache (EVCache=memcached-based), Zuul gateway, Atlas telemetry; Open Connect CDN two-tier pre-positioning (ISP-embedded appliances filled off-peak).
• Uber: H3 hexagonal geo-index (uniform neighbor distances), schemaless (MySQL on HBase pattern), mezzanine rides marketplace matching via Flink streams.
• WhatsApp: Erlang/FreeBSD, 2M connections/server era, mmap-based message store simplicity — minimalism-at-scale counterpoint.
• Instagram/Twitter already covered; Slack: Flannel anycast edge + Vitess sharded MySQL — another Postgres-family proof point.
• Use format: context → constraint → decision → number → lesson; memorize one crisp factoid each for interview garnish.
Synthesizing Case Studies Into Answers

• Never name-drop blindly: tie each case to the QUESTION'S constraint ('like Discord's partition-bucketing, we'd cap channel partitions...').
• Comparison reflex: given prompt, recall nearest case study, ADAPT rather than transplant — differences discussion shows understanding.
• Numbers anchor credibility: partition-size caps, fan-out thresholds, connection densities — one figure per claim suffices.
• Failure-postmortem flavor: what broke FIRST at each company (DB write amplification, GC pauses, hot partitions) — sequence-of-collapse narratives teach design priorities.
• Practice 60-second retellings aloud; polish beats length — five tight cases beat twenty vague ones.
